suite: MacNeal-Harder standard element accuracy tests (beam-relevant subset)
source: R.H. MacNeal & R.L. Harder, 'A Proposed Standard Set of Problems to Test Finite Element Accuracy', Finite Elements in Analysis and Design 1 (1985) 3-20
cross_checked_against: Altair OptiStruct verification OS-V:0720 Straight Cantilever Beam (targets 3.0e-5 / 0.1081 / 0.4321 / 0.03208)
Altair OptiStruct verification OS-V:0710 Curved Cantilever Beam (targets 0.08734 in-plane / 0.5022 out-of-plane)
units: consistent unit system (dimensionless per the paper; treat as in / lb / psi)
note: Targets are the paper's theoretical values and INCLUDE shear deformation. A Bernoulli (Euler) frame element intentionally omits shear deformation: expected converged ratios vs target are 1.0000 (extension), 0.9991 (straight in-plane), ~1.014 (curved in-plane, target also reflects curved/thick-beam theory). 3D cases (out-of-plane + twist) run with the Frame3D element as of FEA Phase 2 Step 4: expected ratios 0.99977 (straight out-of-plane), 0.99654 (curved out-of-plane, both with exact St-Venant J), and 1.0632 for twist — see the twist case's J_provenance note.

models.name: Straight cantilever beam

geometry.J_note: Exact St-Venant series for the 0.2 x 0.1 solid rectangle: J = (16/3)ab^3[1 - (192/pi^5)(b/a) sum_odd tanh(n pi a/2b)/n^5], a=0.1, b=0.05 (half-widths).

models.support: fully fixed at x=0, free at x=6.0

cases.load: unit transverse force at tip, in plane of the 0.2 dimension
unit transverse force at tip, out of plane
cases.closed_form: PL^3/3EI = 0.43200 (bending only, I=1.6667e-5); target incl. shear deformation = 0.4321, expected Bernoulli ratio 0.99977
theta = TL/GJ; with exact St-Venant J = 4.573634e-5 and G = E/2.6 = 3.846154e6, theta = 0.0341085 (ratio 1.0632 vs target)
cases.J_provenance: UNRESOLVED (2026-07-09): the paper's 0.03208 target implies J = TL/(G*theta) = 4.8628e-5, which matches no standard formula for the 0.2 x 0.1 rectangle (exact series 4.5736e-5, thin-plate w/ end correction 4.5775e-5). Altair OS-V:0720 states the target without a J. Element verified exact TL/GJ for both J inputs; engineer may check the original 1985 paper if the 6.3% gap matters.

models.name: Curved cantilever beam (90-degree arc)
models.support: fully fixed at one end, free at the other

cases.load: unit force at tip, in plane, directed radially at the tip (perpendicular to the fixed-end tangent)
cases.closed_form: Bernoulli bending+axial converged limit = pi*P*R^3/(4EI) + pi*P*R/(4EA) = 0.088551; ratio to target 1.0139 (target reflects shear/curved-beam theory)

cases.load: unit force at tip, out of plane
cases.closed_form: Bernoulli bending+torsion converged limit = R^3[(pi/4)/EI_oop + (3pi/4 - 2)/GJ] = 0.500463 with exact J = 4.573634e-5, G = E/2.5 = 4e6; ratio 0.99654 vs target (target adds shear deformation)
